title: Trump’s Hurricane Maria visit to Puerto Rico included paper-towel distribution
description_short: During Trump’s October 2017 Puerto Rico visit after Hurricane Maria, he handed out flashlights and tossed paper-towel rolls to a crowd at a church distributing relief supplies.
description_medium: On October 3, 2017, Trump visited Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria. At a Guaynabo church distributing relief supplies, he handed out flashlights and tossed rolls of paper towels into a crowd, the Associated Press reported. Around 200 people cheered there, and Trump called them “Great people.”
description_long: President Donald Trump visited Puerto Rico on October 3, 2017, after Hurricane Maria struck the island on September 20. The Associated Press reported that Trump toured part of the damage before stopping at a church in Guaynabo being used to distribute relief supplies. The church was in an upscale neighborhood described as among the fastest to recover; around 200 people cheered, and many crowded around him for cellphone photos. Trump handed out flashlights and tossed rolls of paper towels into the crowd. He told those present, “There’s a lot of love in this room, a lot of love,” and called them “Great people.” Earlier in the visit, he praised the federal relief effort and said the job done there was “really nothing short of a miracle.” The AP account described people outside San Juan still struggling to find water and food; it also reported that Puerto Rico’s governor said the official death toll rose from 16 to 34 late that Tuesday. Trump’s itinerary included stops with local residents and service members aboard the USS Kearsarge.

supported_facts: The AP account, published on October 3, 2017, reports Trump’s Puerto Rico visit that Tuesday, after Maria hit the island on September 20.

It reports that Trump toured damage, stopped at a Guaynabo church distributing supplies in a neighborhood described as recovering quickly, and handed out flashlights and tossed paper towels as around 200 people cheered.
It quotes Trump praising the gathering and calling the recovery a miracle; it also describes people still seeking food and water and reports the governor’s then-current death count of 34, up from 16.
It says Trump also visited local residents and service members aboard USS Kearsarge.
